t: Ueda | Castles, Samurai, Sengoku | Britannica
s: July 20, 1998 - Ueda, city, Nagano ken (prefecture), Honshu, Japan. It lies along the Chikuma River. Ueda was a castle town during the Tokugawa period (1603–1867) and later became a centre of silk manufacturing and the site of the Sericultural Professional School. The city’s silk industry declined during the mid-20th century, and synthetic textiles, processed foods, and electrical appliances are now produced.
